mainEntity.name: Is Gojo or Superwhisper better for local dictation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose Gojo when you want a focused local speech-to-text path that returns final text to the field you started in. Choose Superwhisper when you need to configure voice recognition, post-processing, and output modes separately.

Yes. Superwhisper documents configurations with a local voice model and a local language model, or transcription only without post-processing. Its cloud-capable configurations have a different data path.
No. Gojo does not try to replicate a large library of format-specific modes. It is better suited to direct dictated text beside its notch workspace tools.

blocks.label: Short answer
blocks.copy: Choose Gojo for private push-to-talk dictation that is designed to insert final text into the active Mac field, with windows, clipboard, files, media, and system controls nearby. Choose Superwhisper if voice modes, custom formatting, and separately configurable local or cloud model stages are the job.
points: Best for a focused local dictation path: Gojo.
Best for configurable transcription and formatting modes: Superwhisper.
Both need permission and model choices checked before sensitive use.

content.s: Disclosure: Gojo publishes this comparison. We reviewed Gojo's public dictation architecture and Superwhisper's official security documentation on September 4, 2026. Features and model choices can change.

blocks.text: The important difference is the second model stage

content.s: Superwhisper documents two separate stages: speech becomes raw text, then an optional language model can refine or transform it. Either stage can be local or cloud-based. That is useful when an email, meeting note, or custom format needs different treatment. It also means the privacy answer is configuration-specific.

Gojo makes a different trade. Its documented local feature uses an installed local recognizer, applies local transcript policy, then tries to insert only the final result into the original text target. It does not silently switch to a cloud recognizer. Gojo does not offer Superwhisper's broad mode system, and that is a real limitation for people who dictate in several output formats.

blocks.text: Direct insertion has its own safety rules

content.s: For a quick reply or document draft, the endpoint matters more than the transcript window. Gojo captures the focus target before recording and rechecks the application, window, and field before changing anything. It refuses secure fields. If the target changed while you spoke, the documented behavior is to cancel instead of sending the words somewhere new.

items: Gojo says model downloads happen only after a Settings action, not during a dictation shortcut.
Gojo documents local-only recognition, no transcript or audio logging, and no cloud fallback for this feature.
Superwhisper documents a fully local configuration using local voice and language models, or transcription-only mode without language-model processing.
Superwhisper says transcription history is stored locally. Review its retention settings for sensitive material.

items.q: Is Gojo or Superwhisper better for local dictation?

a.s: Choose Gojo for focused local dictation into the original active field. Choose Superwhisper for configurable voice, language-model, and formatting modes.

items.q: Can Superwhisper keep both stages local?

a.s: Yes. Its documentation describes local voice and language-model choices, and a transcription-only path that skips language-model processing.
Gojo does not offer Superwhisper's large mode system or its range of output transformations.
